headline: Fortinet patches critical FortiOS flaws; PHP2Shell exploitation and the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise remain the top open stories

bullets.text: New: Help Net Security reports Fortinet has patched critical FortiOS flaws that were found with AI help. The brief names no CVEs or fixed versions; check Fortinet's advisories for your release.

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is now being successfully exploited in the wild, 4 outlets. Fixes are in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; a third bug, CVE-2026-115560, will not get an emergency fix.
LiteLLM: a leaked master key let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. Version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker stole credentials through Python startup hooks.
CISA's deadline was today (Oct 26) for exploited SQL injection in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-114625) and OS command injection in Collabora Online's CODE server (CVE-2026-110447).

Still open: unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws could let a hacked tailnet device reach root on other servers, and a planted file in a Downloads folder tried to trick an AI coding agent into installing malware.
Breaches: Quest Diagnostics patient personal and health data (3 outlets), 11.7 million CAPCOM ID accounts, and over 70,000 firewall and VPN credentials exposed.

actions: Check Fortinet's advisories and update FortiOS on firewalls and VPN gateways to the fixed release for your branch.
Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and check exposed PHP hosts for compromise.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0. If it ever ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
Patch or take offline Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator and Collabora Online (CODE server), and check both for compromise.
If you use Tailscale SSH, restrict ACLs so only trusted devices can SSH to servers, and watch for Tailscale's fix.
Require approval for installs and shell commands in AI coding agents, and keep them out of untrusted folders like Downloads.
